# Overview
## Package Description

This construct provides the capability for Cloudwatch alarms to trigger alert notifications to slack webhooks.

The construct achieves this by:
* Provisioning an SNS Topic to receive Alert notifications (you can also specific your own SNS Topic if you prefer.)
* Subscribing a Lambda function to publish notifications to a slack webhook

Interested in having this construct support other notifications besides slack?  Please contact the corporate architecture team with details on your use case.  We'd love to help!

# Installation

To install this construct and begin using it in your own CDK stack, first install it into your project:
```
npm install @ps-refarch/alert-notifications
```

# Setup: Enable Slack Webhook & AWS Secrets Manager
Prior to deploying this construct, it is expected that you have configured a slack webhook following our documented process.  In addition, this slack webhook must be added to AWS Secrets Manager in any AWS account where you plan to deploy this construct.

By default, this construct looks for a Secret named "notifications/slack" (or a special subpath that you can specify with the `logicalClientId` property) with the following plaintext contents:
```
{"webhookUrl":"YOUR_SLACK_WEBHOOK_GOES_HERE"}
```

## After Deployment: How Do I Verify that Slack Alerts are Working?
After publishing this construct, it is STRONGLY RECOMMENDED that you test your notifications to verify that chat notifications are being delivered successfully.  The eastiest way to do this is to manually publish an SNS message to your alert topic.

* Log in to your AWS Console, and navigate to the SNS service menu
* Under the "Topics" menu, select the alert topic you wish to use for verification
* Press the "Publish Message" button
* On the message menu, enter a Subject and enter the JSON object below in the "Message body to send to endpoint" field.

```
{
    "NewStateReason":"Test NewStateReason",
    "AlarmName":"Test AlarmName",
    "AlarmDescription":"Test AlarmDescription",
    "StateChangeTime":"Test StateChangeTime",
    "AWSAccountId":"Test AWSAccountId"
}
```

* Lastly, click "Publish Message" and verify that your notification is delivered.  If notifications fail, review Lambda logs for further details.

## Verifying PagerDuty Alerts
PagerDuty requires a more complicated message in order to verify its functionality.  In order to test PD integration, you should use the AWS CLI to simulate an alarm failure.

Instructions can be found here:

https://awscli.amazonaws.com/v2/documentation/api/latest/reference/cloudwatch/set-alarm-state.html

```aws cloudwatch set-alarm-state --alarm-name "myalarm" --state-value ALARM --state-reason "testing purposes"```

## Running this package locally
The following instructions only apply to developers who wish to enhance or maintain this package inside the blueprint-package repository:

In order to run this package's deployment and unit tests locally, you should first perform a root-level yarn install.
```
yarn install
```

After installing dependencies, unit tests can be run from the alert-notificationd directory.
```
npm run test:unit
```

Lastly, a deployable stack has been included in the test/alert-notifications-deploy directory.  This stack can be used for testing out changes locally, and is configured for deployments in the included cdk.json.

```
#After enabling AWS SSO credentials....
npx cdk deploy
```
